response.rationale: The Heberden node at the DIP joint is pathognomonic for osteoarthritis, supported by normal inflammatory markers and negative serologies. The temporal link to vaccination/COVID is nonspecific, and DIP involvement with a bony node is not typical of inflammatory or reactive arthritides.

rejected.why: Negative RF and anti-CCP, DIP involvement atypical for RA
Heberden node is an osteophyte, not a psoriatic feature; no psoriasis or nail changes
Reactive arthritis typically involves lower limbs and lacks Heberden nodes
Back pain and paresthesia are not specific for axial spondyloarthritis; DIP node unexplained
SARS-CoV-2 association is temporal but does not explain chronic Heberden node
Post-vaccination reactive arthritis would not produce a structural Heberden node
